questions.question: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. She is educated than her sister.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.

She is educated than her sister.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "more educated".

Key Points

  • In the given sentence we need to use the "more" in the comparative form to make the sentence grammatically correct.
  • We need to use the comparative form as we are comparing the subject's education to her sister and saying that subject is more educated.
  • We use the comparative form "more" with an adjective.
  • In the given sentence, we use the comparative form more with the adjective "educated" in the given sentence.

The correct sentence is: She is more educated than her sister.

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Mahima is as smarter as Shilpi.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Mahima is as smarter as Shilpi.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 2.

Key Points

  • The phrase "as smart as" is used to make a comparison between two entities, indicating that they possess the same level of intelligence. (उतना ही स्मार्ट जितना)
    • Example: She is as smart as her older brother.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 'as smart as'.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Most smart as (सबसे स्मार्ट जैसा): This phrase is incorrect in English grammar.
    • Example: Incorrect: She is the most smart as her friend.
  • More smart as (ज्यादा स्मार्ट जैसा): This phrase is also incorrect in English grammar.
    • Example: Incorrect: He is more smart as his colleague.
  • Smartest than (सबसे स्मार्ट): This phrase is incorrect because the correct comparative form is "smarter than."
    • Example: Incorrect: She is the smartest than everyone in the class.

questions.question: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. It is my custom to get up early in the morning.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.

It is my custom to get up early in the morning.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2)

Key Points

  • The word "custom" means a traditional and widely accepted way of behaving or doing something that is specific to a particular society, place, or time. (रिवाज)
    • Example: It is a custom in many cultures to celebrate the New Year with fireworks.
  • "Habit" refers to a regular tendency or practice, especially one that is hard to give up. (आदत)
    • Example: Brushing your teeth twice a day is a good habit to maintain oral hygiene.

Hence, we can infer that "habit" is a more suitable word for the given sentence as it refers to a regular practice.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Oddity (विचित्रता): A strange or peculiar person, thing, or trait.
    • Example: His habit of wearing mismatched socks is considered an oddity by his friends.
  • Addiction (लत): The fact or condition of being addicted to a particular substance, thing, or activity.
    • Example: His addiction to video games is affecting his studies.
  • Perfection (पूर्णता): The condition, state, or quality of being free or as free as possible from all flaws or defects.
    • Example: She strives for perfection in everything she does.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence. Rohit is write to them three times.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence.

Rohit is write to them three times.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 2..

Key Points

  • The word "write" means to mark (letters, words, or other symbols) on a surface, typically paper, with a pen, pencil, or similar implement. (लिखना)
    • Example: She likes to write in her journal every night.
  • "written" is the past participle of "write" and is used to indicate that an action was completed at some point in the past. (लिखा हुआ)
    • Example: The letter was written by her last week.

Hence, we can infer that the correct form to use in the given sentence is 'has written'.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Rohit had write (रोहित ने लिखा था): This is grammatically incorrect because "had" should be followed by the past participle "written".
    • Example: Incorrect: Rohit had write to them.
  • Rohit was beings written (रोहित लिखा जा रहा था): This is grammatically incorrect and makes no sense in the context.
    • Example: Incorrect: Rohit was beings written to them.
  • Rohit was write (रोहित लिख रहा था): This is also grammatically incorrect because "was" should be followed by the gerund form "writing".
    • Example: Incorrect: Rohit was write to them.

questions.question: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement'. The prisoners are kept at constant surveillance.

The prisoners are kept at constant surveillance.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'kept under'.

Key Points

  • Here, 'kept under' should be used instead of 'kept at'.

    • Example: The police kept her/the building under surveillance.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. The inspector smile after he was finished and patted Margie’s head.

  • "Smiled" is the past tense of "smile", indicating that the action has already happened. (मुस्कुराया)

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select ‘No substitution required’. Hears to the news tonight at 9 p.m., as there will be an important announcement about the budget.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select ‘No substitution required’.

Hears to the news tonight at 9 p.m., as there will be an important announcement about the budget.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Listen to'.

Key Points

  • The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
  • Here, 'Listen to' should be used instead of 'Hears to'.
  • 'Hearing' is an event; it is something that happens to us as a natural process. 'Listening' is an action; it is something we do consciously.
  • Example:
    • Suddenly I heard a noise. Someone was in the garden. 
    • I listened very carefully to what she said and wrote it all down. 
  • In the given context, 'Listen to' should be used because listening to the news is an action which we do consciously.
  • Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is Option 4.
     

Correct Sentence: Listen to the news tonight at 9 p.m., as there will be an important announcement about the budget.

Hinglish

  • दिया गया वाक्य व्याकरण की दृष्टि से गलत है।
  • यहाँ, 'Hear to' के स्थान पर 'Listen to' का प्रयोग किया जाना चाहिए।
  • 'Hearing' एक घटना है; यह कुछ ऐसा है जो एक प्राकृतिक प्रक्रिया के रूप में हमारे साथ होता है। 'Listening' एक Verb है; यह कुछ ऐसा है जो हम होशपूर्वक करते हैं।
  • Example:
    • Suddenly I heard a noise. Someone was in the garden. (Hear)
    • I listened very carefully to what she said and wrote it all down. (Listen)
  • दिए गए सन्दर्भ में 'Listen to' का प्रयोग करना चाहिए क्योंकि क्योंकि समाचार सुनना एक ऐसी क्रिया है जो हम होशपूर्वक करते हैं।
  • इसलिए, ऊपर वर्णित बिंदुओं के अनुसार, हम पाते हैं कि सही उत्तर विकल्प 4 है।

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Reading has the capacity to make a man wise, but reading of only textbooks is like living in room of our same height.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Reading has the capacity to make a man wise, but reading of only textbooks is like living in room of our same height.

options.text: Reading should make a man wise
options.html: Reading should make a man wise

options.text: Reading shall make a man wise
options.html: Reading shall make a man wise

questions.solution:
The correct answer is "Reading makes a man wise"

Key Points

  • The most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence is: "Reading has the capacity to make a man wise."
  • This option correctly conveys the intended meaning of the original sentence that reading has the potential or ability to make a person wise.
  • Option 2 is incorrect as it does not use the correct subject-verb agreement (make should be changed to makes to agree with the singular subject "Reading").
  • Option 3 and 4 are also incorrect as they suggest an obligation or a certainty that reading will make a man wise, which is not necessarily true.
  • The original sentence is suggesting that reading has the potential to make a person wise, but that potential is limited if one only reads textbooks, like living in a room of the same height, implying that one needs to read more broadly to truly gain wisdom.
  • Thus, option 1 is the correct answer.


Correct Sentence: Reading makes a man wise, but reading of only textbooks is like living in room of our same height.

  • "Carry on" refers to continuing with an activity or task. (जारी रखना)

Hence, in the context of the sentence, "carry on" is the most appropriate substitution for "carry out" when referring to continuing a business in someone’s absence.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Carry at (ले जाना): This is not a correct phrase in English.

  • Carry in (अंदर ले जाना): This phrase refers to bringing something inside.
    • Example: He asked the movers to carry in the furniture.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement required’. questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3)

Key Points

  • The word "promote" means to support or actively encourage something; to advance or raise to a higher position or rank. (बढ़ावा देना)

  • "Traditional" refers to something that is based on customs, beliefs, or methods that have existed for a long time without changing. (पारंपरिक)

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Option 1: promotes sharing of tradition (परंपरा का साझा करना बढ़ावा देता है): This phrase is not grammatically correct as "tradition" is a noun and does not fit well in the context.

  • Option 2: promotes sharing of traditionally (पारंपरिक रूप से साझा करने को बढ़ावा देता है): The adverb "traditionally" does not fit correctly in this context.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. The plant will die unless you will water it every day.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

The plant will die unless you will water it every day.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'water'.

Key Points   

  • The error lies incorrect usage of future tense i.e. 'will'.
  • Let's take a look at the word 'unless' it means the same as if...not. Like if, unless is followed by a present tense, a past tense, or a past perfect tense (never by a conditional). Unless is used instead of if...not in conditional sentences of all types. The order of the clauses doesn't matter with sentences using unless.
  • Unless is never followed by future tense.
  • Example: 
    •  You'll be sick unless you stop eating.
  • Thus, 'water' will be used in place of 'will water'.

Correct sentence: The plant will die unless you water it every day.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. The patient was suggested to cut off on the daily intake of carbs.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’.

The patient was suggested to cut off on the daily intake of carbs.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: cut down.

Key Points

  • "Cut down" is the correct phrasal verb to use when advising someone to reduce the amount of something, such as food intake, in this case, carbohydrates.
    • For example: Rohit cut down fatty food recently.
  • "Cut off" does not correctly convey the intended meaning of reducing intake; instead, it implies completely removing or severing connections.
  • Therefore, to accurately convey the advice given to the patient about reducing the intake of carbs, "cut down on" is the appropriate choice.

Hence, the correct sentence should be: The patient was suggested to cut down on the daily intake of carbs.

questions.question: Choose an appropriate word that can substitute the bracketed word and complete the sentence meaningfully. Shelley was very happy (while) I accepted her invitation to her birthday party.
questions.questionHtml:

questions.solution:

Key Points

  • The word "while" means during the time that; at the same time as. (जबकि)
    • Example: She read a book while waiting for the bus.
  • "when" refers to at or during the time that. (जब)
    • Example: He was very happy when he heard the news.
  • Hence, we can infer that the word 'when' is an appropriate substitute for 'while' in the context of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is: when.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • As (जैसे): Used to indicate that something happens during the time that something else is happening.

  • After (बाद में): Following in time.
    • Example: She went for a walk after lunch.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Once the seminar was over, the host gave up the certificates to the active participants.

questions.solution:

Key Points

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • brought about (लाना): To cause something to happen.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required.' These days I like to eat nuts and seeds along with fruits as I'm conscious of my healthfulness .
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required.'

These days I like to eat nuts and seeds along with fruits as I'm conscious of my healthfulness.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'health'.

Key Points

  • The given sentence is contextually incorrect.
  • Here, 'health' should be used instead of 'healthfulness'.
  • Though 'Healthfulness' is a noun, it defines the quality of promoting good health, which is not accurate  according to the given context. As per context 'health' will be correct as it defines - a state of complete physical, mental, and social well-being.
  • Thus, according to the given context 'health' will be the correct option and therefore the answer.

Note- In the given sentence one wants to convey that he is conscious of his well-being, healthiness, fitness, etc

Correct Sentence: These days I like to eat nuts and seeds along with fruits and I'm conscious of my health.

Hinglish

  • दिया गया वाक्य व्याकरण की दृष्टि से गलत है।
  • यहां 'healthfulness' के स्थान पर 'health' का प्रयोग करना चाहिए।
  • 'Healthfulness' एक noun है जिसका अर्थ है 'शरीर या मन के स्वास्थ्य के लिए लाभकारी'।
  • जबकि दिए गए संदर्भ में 'noun' की आवश्यकता होती है।
  • Adjective वे शब्द होते हैं जो noun के होने के गुण या अवस्था का वर्णन करते हैं। यहां, ऐसी किसी योग्यता की आवश्यकता नहीं है।
  • इसलिए, 'health' का प्रयोग करना चाहिए।

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence. There was a noise that was wake me up.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’. The rising prices of essential food items have placed (a/an) weighty burden on the poor.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence. Losing my job turned out to be an unexpected benefit because it pushed me to start my own business, which has been more successful than I ever imagined.
questions.questionHtml:

Losing my job turned out to be an unexpected benefit because it pushed me to start my own business, which has been more successful than I ever imagined.

The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. "a blessing in disguise".

Key Points

    • Example: Having a big family is a mixed blessing; you get a lot of love but also a lot of responsibilities.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined part of the following sentence. Mathew decided to complete the marathon to prove that he is still fit as a fiddle in his eighties.

questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate segment to substitute the underlined wordsin the given sentence.

After he leave, we discussed his suggestion.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3)

Key Points

  • In the given sentence, the correct past perfect tense 'he had left' is used.
  • This indicates that the action of leaving was completed before the discussion took place.
  • Past perfect tense is used to describe an action that was completed before another action in the past.
  • Therefore, the correct form is 'he had left'.

Hence, the correct sentence is  "After he had left, we discussed his suggestion."

Additional Information

  • The past perfect tense is formed by using 'had' + past participle of the verb.
  • It is often used with a time expression such as 'after', 'before', 'when', etc. to show the sequence of events.
    • Example: She had finished her homework before she went out to play.
